taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: Drawn as a shrub on the conifers' program: Abrams (1923 p. 77) gives the alpine plants as a "Low or usually prostrate alpine or arctic shrub, forming patches several feet in diameter"; several stems lean out from one foot and spread low.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "most often grows as a low, decumbent mat-forming shrub reaching up to 4.9 feet (1.5 m) in height"; var. montana, the alpine form, "usually less than 3 feet (0.9 m) tall".

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: mats 10 cm to 50 cm high in subalpine heath, as in the photos; Abrams (1923 p. 77): "Low or usually prostrate".

traits.crown_width_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "reaching up to 4.9 feet (1.5 m) in height and 7.6 to 13.1 feet (2-4 m) across".

traits.stem_posture.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: "Low or usually prostrate alpine or arctic shrub, forming patches several feet in diameter".

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "Individuals can live for more than 170 years".

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "a native, evergreen shrub or columnar tree".

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "a native, evergreen shrub".

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: leaves in whorls along the branches: no rosette.

traits.bark_texture.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "The bark of common juniper is thin, shreddy or scaly, often exfoliating into thin strips".

traits.leaf_form.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "Unlike most junipers, whose leaves turn scalelike at maturity, common juniper leaves remain needlelike throughout the shrub's life"; the Dendrology extraction (facts.csv, dendrology-2026-10-14#3148) also gives needle.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: "Leaves in whorls of 3, ascending".

traits.leaves_per_whorl.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: "Leaves in whorls of 3"; FEIS (Tirmenstein 1999): "arranged in whorls of 3".

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: leaves "linear-lanceolate"; read as linear, as the genus (p. 76) gives them "linear-subulate".

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: leaves "pungently acute".

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: no teeth described: a needle "keeled or strongly convex on the lower surface, deeply grooved above".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: leaves "6-12 mm. long".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: needles 1 mm to 1.5 mm wide, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: needles kept 5 to 10 years; Abrams's genus (1923 p. 76) says only "Leaves persistent for many years".

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: cones from about 5 to 15 years old on a low shrub; no source read gives it.

traits.sexual_system.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "Common juniper is typically dioecious but occasionally monoecious"; the Dendrology extraction (dendrology-2026-10-14#3148) gives dioecious.

traits.cone_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: "berries globose, 7-9 mm. broad", so as long as broad; the Dendrology extraction (dendrology-2026-10-14#3148) gives (4-)7-9(-13) mm across.

traits.cone_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 77, Juniperus sibirica: berries "bright blue, covered with a white bloom"; sRGB by eye from the photos (pale glaucous blue).

traits.cone_maturation_years.note: FEIS species review, Juniperus communis (Tirmenstein 1999): "Seed usually matures during the second growing season".

traits.cone_retention_years.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: ripe berry-cones mostly fall or are eaten within the year they ripen, as the template's.

generator.params.note: Rocky Mountain juniper's (juniperus-scopulorum) values, changed by hand for the prostrate alpine common juniper: five stems from one foot leaning far out (stem_angle 75), short level branches that turn up little, slow height growth, and branches kept close to the ground (ground_gap 0.005) so the mat is not shed where it lies (Abrams 1923 p. 77: "Low or usually prostrate"; FEIS: "low, decumbent mat-forming shrub"). The needles' life comes from leaf_life_years by the Pinidae rule. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: 0.35 m tall at 30 years in the open, a low mat as in the photos; FEIS gives up to 1.5 m. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, spreading mat of stiff, sharp, upcurved needles in threes, grey-green with a white band above, carrying pale glaucous blue berry-cones. Organ cards from Rocky Mountain juniper's (juniperus-scopulorum), recoloured and resized by hand. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).
